neighborhood_overview:
This apartment is located in Psirri, minutes walk away from Monastiraki and Plaka.

Monastiraki station serves the Athens International airport and the port of Piraeus.

Plaka is the heart of Athens historical city centre, where most main monuments are located.

Psirri is a place where you still find lovely artisan shops such as candle making and leather work shops. It has great restaurants, cafes, art spaces and an outdoor cinema where you can enjoy films in the original language.

You will also find grocery stores, bakeries and the Athens Central Food Market, the famous Varvakios Market.

Walking around Psirri can be deceiving as it has many old buildings and lots of street art. The street art scene has produced many outstanding artists and their work is widely photographed and admired.

The artisan shops, the residents who greet each other by their first names and the visitors create a place of unique character.

host_about:
Who would have thought when I boarded a plane for Greece more than 20 years ago, planning on backpacking through the mountains and then heading north through then Yugoslavia I'd end up making Greece my second home?
But here I am, 20 something years later, running a fabulous Greek vacation rental business with historic homes & penthouses in Athens, planning Greek travel itineraries and leading small group food & wine focused tours around my adopted homeland and loving the life that I am lucky enough to be living. Of course I did pick up an equally crazy, workaholic Greek husband along the way, as well as a stray Greek animal or two!

Update: End of November 2017 .... This year Basil and I celebrate 15 years opening our Greek vacation rentals to guests from around the world. All these years we've been hopping between Basil's home city, Athens and Carole's home city of Chicago.  Time and time again guests in Greece ask us if they can stay in our Chicago home while we're in Athens.... so we're finally doing it - we've just completed the renovation of a fab old factory with 3 vacation rentals called the Magic Factory Lofts. We've got 3 and 4 bedroom homes in the heart of the city with Big Shoulders -  in our hybrid warehouse (which in a previous life housed a bar and a dance hall, followed by a costume and magic card factory and then a photography studio where probably every Butterball turkey advertisement in the 1980s was shot .... the photos, not the turkeys!)

So come stay with us ... and then stay with us again. Whether we share an ouzo in Athens in our Acropolis View Alpha Plus penthouse or Sky Villa or a beer and a hot dog in Chicago, in our Magic Factory Lofts  we know that you won't be disappointed.

Update: End of November 2017 .... This year Basil and I celebrate 15 years opening our Greek vacation rentals to guests from around the world. neighborhood_overview:
Off the beaten tourist track and centrally located, Victoria square is perhaps Athens’ most multicultural neighbourhood. Originally an upper class district of Athens and then a cultural center for theatre and music in the 60s, it sadly fell into disarray in the 80s and 90s as old locals ventured to the cooler hillsides surrounding Athens. Subsequent low rents attracted newcomers to the city and in recent years, artists, creatives and students have moved in, making this the center of Athens’ newest gentrification wave.
Drink an arabic coffee, have a greek ouzo, have a fancy cocktail at our local bar 'Match Point' (for Woody Allen fans) or 'Village' in nearby Agiou Georgiou square. Or take in an art show in the many new galleries popping up around the area - this neighborhood is for those that want to explore the contemporary and creative side of Athens.

name: Studio with Acropolis view
description:
Stylish 6th floor studio - with independent roof entrance and access- in the heart of Athens, one min walk from old stadium, and breathaking panoramic views of the Acropolis, the old Stadium, Mt Lycabettus.
Easy access to all public transport.

The space
The studio is a space of 50 sq.m with a king size bed, a bathroom with shower and its own living room area and kitchenette, which opens up to an unbelievably large private terrace with an amazing view of the Acropolis and the old Olympic Stadium.
It is ideal for 2 people.

Guest access
The studio is connected to a 5th floor flat but there is a hatch that separates one floor from the other and offers full privacy. You will have your own private entrance on the 6th floor and full access to a huge garden terrace that overlooks the old stadium, the Acropolis and Mount Lycabettus.
The studio and terrace will be ALL YOURS during your stay.

Other things to note
neighborhood_overview: The flat is on Eratosthenous St, in the 'Kallimarmaro' area (another word for the old stadium) and is very cool area with amazing little tavernas (such as Stavros round the back of the building) that serve delicious Greek food at very reasonable prices, as well as bakeries that you can get lovely pies for breakfast. If you walk up to the top of the road you will find some cute bars with personality and a cool crowd.
host_about:
I am Greek but have been living abroad for years (London, Paris) - currently living in London. 
I am an avid traveller that enjoys getting to know places from the perspective of a local - in my opinion it's the only way to to get to know the real feel of the place. I am very friendly, clean and tidy and when visiting new places, staying in flats with character; always adds to the experience! 

While I am away, with the help of my mother Maria, we are renting out a space in Athens which, if anyone is visiting, should consider staying there because it is superbly located, designed beautifully and has wonderful views of the Acropolis and the old Olympic Stadium - some of the lovely things you should share with other travellers! ;-)
I also recently added my island home which if you are wanting to experience 'real' Greek island life (vs touristy commercial islands) .... this is the place. :-)

neighborhood_overview:
Psirri is a very special neighborhood.
In the beginning of the century, poor families from the aegean islands used to come here for work and built small houses. There is still a community of Naxos' people with small restaurants with live music and their traditional products such as cheese, seafood and goat's meat.
Another community of Psirri were the leather workers, making shoes and leather accessories, so there are still many manufacturers where you can buy or even order your own leather goods. These people worked in big industrial buildings built in Psirri during the '60s and '70s.
And last but most importantly, Psirri is surrounded by archeological sites The Acropolis, the Ancient Agora, the Cemetery of Keramikos. All in 3-10 minutes walk.
So, there is not only one way to describe Psirri. The diversity of it's character is what makes it so special and interesting.

neighborhood_overview:
Psirri is a very special neighborhood.
In the beginning of the century, poor families from the aegean islands used to come here for work and built small houses. There is still a community of Naxos' people with small restaurants with live music and their traditional products such as cheese, seafood and goat's meat.
Another community of Psirri were the leather workers, making shoes and leather accessories, so there are still many manufacturers where you can buy or even order your own leather goods. These people worked in big industrial buildings built in Psirri during the '60s and '70s.
And last but most importantly, Psirri is surrounded by archeological sites The Acropolis, the Ancient Agora, the Cemetery of Keramikos. All in 3-10 minutes walk.
So, there is not only one way to describe Psirri. The diversity of it's character is what makes it so special and interesting.

so you are old by the time you reach the island,
wealthy with all you have gained on the way,
not expecting Ithaka to make you rich.
 
Ithaka gave you the marvelous journey.
Without her you would not have set out.
She has nothing left to give you now.
 
And if you find her poor, Ithaka won’t have fooled you.
Wise as you will have become, so full of experience,
you will have understood by then what these Ithakas mean. 

Ithaka-C. P. Cavafy (greek poetry)

I wish you a wonderful stay!

Best,

Athina

Metaxourgeio is one of the Athens’ most fascinating neighborhoods. Lying roughly north west of the city center, it takes its name from the traditional industry that once populated the area: literally, the ‘silk factory’. This lively neighborhood is undergoing a slow, but significantly more refined process of gentrification and is now the undisputed cultural heart of the city.
As ever, it started when galleries and artists began to move there. Beautiful neoclassical houses and spacious old abandoned warehouses proved ideal for galley owners, artists, performers and creators.
Then came the young entrepreneurs and industrial-style bars like BIOS, restaurants like Polly Magoo, Aleria or Varoulko and cultural institutions like The Breeder project, often combining the area’s traditionally mixed ethnic heritage with Hellenic influences – reinventing and revitalizing the area in the process.

host_about:
My name is Eftihia (Eftehea), from the words 'ef' and 'tihi' (tehe) which mean 'good' and 'luck' in ancient greek. My name is also a noun. In modern greek the word eftihia means happiness. For ancient greeks happy was the fortunate one. Nowdays happy is the joyful one. My name is quite a heavy thing to go by everyday, as it means something so great and simple (but veeeery complicated too..), that it is sometimes a real struggle to deliver its meaning and idea and project in in your life. And other's lives around you.

My parents origins are from the Peloponese and Zakynthos (Ionian Island). But I grew up in the wider terretory of Attica Prefecture, in particular in 2 suberbs of Athens- Marousi and Kifisia.

My profession is acting and as that started as a career (B.C. - before Crisis!!!) but has practically ended up a practical hobby (A.C.- after Crisis..), I am trying to reinvent myself and my life and scetch a 'plan B'..

Whatever that will occur to be, my true passion is walking barefoot on sharp rocks of isolated greek islands. If I was from India I think they would say I used to be a wild goat in a previous life. My technique in this strange extreme sport is really something to admire. I love walking in general, I like nature and even though I am definately a child of the city, my soul meets its 'core' when away from it. It is like the purity of my existence absolutely relates to the inviroment I find myself in. The landscape of a mountain or a beach or a lake or a river automatically turns me into a better person. My effort has always been to manage to carry that person with me even in the packed and trafficy Streets and Avenues of Athens.

My favourite time of the day in the area I leave in (where my house that welcomes airbnb guests is located) is between 2-6 in the morning. When the city sleeps one is able to 'pick up' and fully absorb this area's true energy. When crowded it is just another touristic place with great historical interest. But its healing effect one can only get when it is (Website hidden by Airbnb) and (Website hidden by Airbnb) l.. At times of grief, pressure or distress I found that walking (AND jogging too!) around in that neighbourhood at these hours of the day was very therapeutic.

Sharing your house with people you don't know (and- at circummstances- you might actually never even meet!!!) became possible thanks to this whole airbnb notion that you created. It is a beautiful chain that connects people who wanted more- out of traveling- than a regular hotel or rudimantary furnished/equipped apartments. That chain allows travellers to make a 'subtour'  in their tour, experience how a person from a different country and culture lives. Like a quick whimsy eavesdropping or innocent peeping that might 'salt or sweeten up' the first and last moments of ones journey to a foreign place. 

So.. Long live the AirBnB!

neighborhood_overview: The area took its name from the city square or dēmos (δῆμος) of the Kerameis (Κεραμεῖς, potters), which in turn derived its name from the word κέραμος (kéramos, "pottery clay", from which the English word "ceramic" is derived). The "Inner Kerameikos" was the former "potters' quarter" within the city and "Outer Kerameikos" covers the cemetery and also the Dēmósion Sēma (δημόσιον σῆμα, public graveyard) just outside the city walls, where Pericles delivered his funeral oration in 431 BC. The cemetery was also where the Ηiera Hodos (the Sacred Way, i.e. the road to Eleusis) began, along which the procession moved for the Eleusinian Mysteries.

neighborhood_overview:
Strefi Hill is located in the neighborhood of Exarcheia in Athens, Greece northwest of mount Lykavittos.
It used to belong to the wealthy Strefis family. In the 19th and early 20th centuries, a stone quarry operated here, but in the 1920s its operation was suspended and trees were planted on the hill. In 1963, the Strefis family handed over the hill to the city of Athens. Strefi Hill is above Exarcheia. Exarcheia is a very interesting neighbourhood full of history. Exarcheia (Greek: Εξάρχεια) is in downtown Athens, Greece close to the historical building of the National Technical University of Athens. The Exarcheia region is famous as a home for Greek anarchists. It took the name from a merchant named Exarchos (Greek: Έξαρχος) who opened a large general store there. Exarcheia is bordered on the east by Kolonaki and is framed by Patission Street, Panepistimiou Street and Alexandras Avenue.

There is a Greek word, "filoxenia", which means, roughly, "friendship to strangers".  Every Greek has this concept genetically linked by the mitochondria:  Mama always taught us to be nice to people.  Greeks will, sometimes grumbling all the way, drive miles out of their way at rush hour, knowing they will be late for work because a stranger asks where the airport is.

My motto, learned from a professor in college, is "Good enough isn't".

The Monastiraki and Psirri neighborhood is a commercial center during the day but is transformed to a popular nightspot during the evening.

Our company  Ma Maison Y&R owns four luxury apartments in Athens.
We are Yannis and Rena, "fellow travelers" for the last twenty years. Four years ago we decided to do something that we love very much, through BOOKING. 
The Greek word "ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΙΑ=hospitality" is of a particular importance in the Greek culture. It’s a compound word from "ΦΙΛΩ=LOVE" and "ΞΕΝΟΣ=GUEST " and refers to the act of nestling and caring of a guest by the host. It was an institution for the ancient Greeks to welcome and take care of the guests at their home. They believed particularly in the idea of hospitality and regarded it as a moral duty and a sacred rule of the gods (Xenios Zeus was the protector of the guests). They offered them bath and sleep and they greeted them with gifts. The host and the guest were linked with friendly ties, which where inherited to their descendants. 
This is our inheritance.
It will be an honor to host you.

There are two kinds of and the famous large venues playing electronic/dance music and famous bouzoukia, which are venues where Greek singers perform live. Tripodon street is considered as the oldest street of Athens. It is located in the same place as it was 25 centuries ago and has the same name since then.

The Way of Glory
The very precious story of Tripodon Street begins from the fact that it was, perhaps, the broadest street of ancient Athens (six meters wide) and the shortest one to go from the theater of Dionysus to the Agora. It was not done to serve the city's traffic, but to get the Athenians to watch the theatrical performances of Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides and Aristophanes. It was the street of Art, the Philosophers, the Theater, the Architecture, the Greek Thought. In this way the torch relaying took place in honor of the god Dionysus.

The district of Exarcheia was created between 1870 and 1880 at the confines of the city and has played a significant role in the social and political life of Greece.
It is here that the Athens Polytechnic uprising of November 1973 took place.
Exarcheia is a place where many intellectuals and artists live.
It's close to the historical building of the National Technical University of Athens, the famous National Archaeological Museum of Athens and Strefis hill.
It is a lively, artistic and cultural neighborhood full of diversity.

Neoclassical buildings line the streets, that other than residences, they host several cultural and archaeological institutions, galleries and embassies. Small restaurants, known as “mezedopolia” with live Greek music are hidden in the narrow streets of Exarhia. Underground bars and night clubs for all music tastes can be discovered here.
At the area you can also find many computer shops, used vinyl and CD shops, terrific guitar shops, used bookshops, boutiques. Many Greek artists, poets and writers are living around. host_about:
ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

neighborhood_overview: This mostly transient neighborhood, from tourist-central Plaka to more residential districts of Athens, like Neos Kosmos and Petralona, was named after a pre-World War II bed-manufacturing factory that was owned by a businessman named Koukakis. The district lies at the base of Lofos Filopappou (Filopappos Hill), also known as the Lofos Mousseon (Hill of the Muses, as legend has it that the nine Muses were buried there). The name of the hill, Filopappou was the nickname that Gauis Julius was known by. The rough translation of Filopappou means “favourite grandson of his grandfather”. Gaius Julius' grandfather was in fact the last King of Kommagene, Antiochus IV. A number of pleasant paths lead from streets at the base of Filopappos up through its pine-clad slopes, some ending at the Dora Stratou Theater or the observatory.

neighborhood_overview: This apartment is located in Psirri, minutes walk away from Monastiraki and Plaka. Monastiraki station serves the Athens International airport and the port of Piraeus. Plaka is the heart of Athens historical city centre, where most main monuments are located. Psirri is a place where you still find lovely artisan shops such as candle making and leather work shops. It has great restaurants, cafes, art spaces and an outdoor cinema where you can enjoy films in the original language. You will also find grocery stores, bakeries and the Athens Central Food Market, the famous Varvakios Market. Walking around Psirri can be deceiving as it has many old buildings and lots of street art. The street art scene has produced many outstanding artists and their work is widely photographed and admired. The artisan shops, the residents who greet each other by their first names and the visitors create a place of unique character.

neighborhood_overview:
The Monastiraki and Psirri neighborhood is a commercial center during the day but is transformed to a popular nightspot during the evening.
The cosmopolitanism of the city is evident as locals, tourists and immigrants all intermingle in the vicinity.
Miaouli Street is primarily a trading place for leather and footwear items during the day, with various cafes and small restaurants providing an outlook to the local commercial activities. From the early afternoon, however, the cafes, restaurants, and bars attract a wide variety of people who want to smoke nargileh (oriental tobacco pipe), eat mezze (selection of small dishes) and drink tsipouro or have a drink and dance at the bars. Finally, in recent years Athens has become a sort of graffiti Mecca and the neighborhood is one of the main areas in Athens where one can observe the transformation of old or abandoned buildings by young street artists.
host_about:
My name is Stratis and I grew up in Athens. I have traveled extensively and lived in England, the US, Syria and Lebanon while studying Anthropology and History. 
I returned to Athens just when the financial crisis struck hard and I have found myself being involved in the Miaouli8 project. Miaouli8 is a collection of lofts and spaces situated in an industrial building built by my grandfather in the mid 1960s.
The listings that I am hosting are the outcome of an inventive effort to revive the unused spaces of the building. Using old family furniture, second hand vintage objects from flea markets and a lot of personal work, we have transformed these former craft spaces into modern Athenian apartments.

Our company  Ma Maison Y&R owns four luxury apartments in Athens.
We are Yannis and Rena, "fellow travelers" for the last twenty years. Four years ago we decided to do something that we love very much, through BOOKING. 
The Greek word "ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΙΑ=hospitality" is of a particular importance in the Greek culture. It’s a compound word from "ΦΙΛΩ=LOVE" and "ΞΕΝΟΣ=GUEST " and refers to the act of nestling and caring of a guest by the host. It was an institution for the ancient Greeks to welcome and take care of the guests at their home. They believed particularly in the idea of hospitality and regarded it as a moral duty and a sacred rule of the gods (Xenios Zeus was the protector of the guests). They offered them bath and sleep and they greeted them with gifts. The host and the guest were linked with friendly ties, which where inherited to their descendants. 
This is our inheritance.
It will be an honor to host you.

TopHouzzing’s story is simple yet exciting! We are Maria & Alex, the founders, both engineers. So we were already working together in the design & construction sector, so we  dealt with properties all the time. We are both into details, both love doing something right from scratch.

While we were traveling to new places and meeting old friends / making new ones, we felt what a rental should feel like, what it should offer guests like ourselves. Lots were missing, especially the simple little things that makes a visitor feel right at home -away from home. We then decided to start a rentals & real estate management company. It was July 2015 and we named it TopHouzzing Properties - the mission was simply to offer truly top accommodation to our guests. Starting then with a couple of our own properties, refurbished completely, we embarked on a great journey. 

Today the company manages close to 100 properties and growing steadily, mostly in Athens but also in mainland Greece and islands, flats, villas and so on. TopHouzzing  also offers consulting & real estate, design & construction and other professional services in its portfolio.

Hard work and our passion paid off. Our success is clearly stated not only in the many owners that trust us with their properties but even more in the hundreds 5-star reviews from guests from all over the world,  leading us to have a record of 14 consecutive quarters-since the company’s inception- SuperHost status on Airbnb!

We take very good care of our guests and so do we with owners. You see, we both think as guests & owners ourselves. We are waiting anxiously to host you or to manage your property, in both cases you are in good hands with us.

Ταξιδεύω απο πολύ νωρίς στη ζωή μου, έζησα 4 χρόνια στην Ν. Υόρκη στη δεκαετία του '80, είμαι δασκάλα χορού και ψυχοθεραπεύτρια. Έχω δημιουργήσει η ίδια, σχεδιάζοντας, διακοσμώντας και επιβλέποντας την ανακατασκευή κτισμάτων, όπως το στούντιό μου και το σπίτι μου.  Ξέρω έτσι τη διαδικασία της δημιουργίας και πόσο κόπο και χρήματα απαιτεί. Σέβομαι, είμαι υπεύθυνη ως προς τον χώρο  και μ' αρέσει να ζω σε όμορφο αισθητικά περιβάλλον με ενδιαφέροντες ανθρώπους. Δεν καπνίζω και προσπαθώ να ζω υγιεινά. Χρειάζομαι η κατοικία που βρίσκομαι να είναι καθαρή, να έχει τάξη αλλά και προσωπικότητα. Το σημαντικότερο όλων όμως για μένα είναι η θετική αλληλεπίδραση και η καλή επικοινωνία με τους ανθρώπους που έρχομαι σ' επαφή. Αγαπώ τις διαφορετικές κουλτούρες και εμπνέομαι απο την τέχνη, τον πολιτισμό. Είμαι αυτόνομος και συνεννοήσιμος άνθρωπος. Ζω μια γεμάτη ζωή στην πόλη μου.
Δεν μπορώ να ζω χωρίς την τέχνη, τη φύση, τις ζεστές σχέσεις, την ομορφιά, την αλλαγή και την εξέλιξη. Πηγαίνω τακτικά σε ταινίες κυρίως σινεφίλ, ακούω μουσική απο κλασική, μέχρι τζαζ, ροκ, ethnic, alternative rock, διαβάζω λογοτεχνία, ψυχολογία και ιστορία. Κάνω διαλογισμό μέσα απο την κίνηση για μένα και διδάσκοντας η ίδια-έχω εκπαιδεύσει πολύ κόσμό 27 χρόνια τώρα στην Ελλάδα και στο εξωτερικό. Θα με βρείτε σχετικά στο (Website hidden by Airbnb) Ως προς το φαγητό, χρειάζομαι η όμορφη γεύση να συνδυάζεται με υγιεινή διατροφή, προσπαθώ να μην τρώω συχνά κρέας και να αποφεύγω τα γαλακτοκομικά. Ως επισκέπτης είμαι υπεύθυνη, προσαρμόσιμη  και ξέρω να βάζω τα όρια μου όταν βλέπω πως μια κατάσταση δεν ανταποκρίνεται σε αυτό που χρειάζομαι. Ως οικοδεσπότης προσφέρω φροντίδα και φιλική επικοινωνία ώστε να νοιώσει ο άλλος άνετα. Βοηθάω τον ξένο σε αυτά που χρειάζεται και ακούω τις ανάγκες του. Του δίνω χώρο να γνωρίσει την καθημερινότητά μου ανάλογα με τη σχέση που έχω μαζί του. Ουσιαστικά κάθε φορά χρειάζεται να "μετράω" την απόσταση που κάνει και τους δύο να αισθάνονται όμορφα και λειτουργικά. Pangrati is at the epicentre of Athens’ rebirth, with its unique mix of older residential buildings and new restaurants, bars and boutiques adding to the already numerous tavernas and cafes long popular with locals. We chose to make Pangrati home because of its unique mix of old Athenian neighbourhood charm - and the local shops and services to serve its long time residents - with some of the city’s most modern nightspots and boutiques. For those seeking to sample the emergent Athenian contemporary culture scene, Pangrati plays host to some of the city’s most on-trend restaurants, cafes and bars, museums and galleries. A simple taverna meal, or an arthouse film and cocktails ‘til dawn, the choice is yours. All of this is but a few minutes’ walking distance to most of the city’s major cultural attractions, but blissfully free of the tourist crowds.

Psirri is a place where you still find lovely artisan shops such as candle making and leather work shops. It has great restaurants, cafes, art spaces and an outdoor cinema where you can enjoy films in the original language.

host_about:
Vaso‘s house is located in Ano Patissia, approximately 3 km from the center of Athens and in proximity to public transport stations (bus and metro).

Patissia is a historic district of Athens. At the end of the 19th and the beginning of the 20th century many wealthy Athenians chose this area to built their summer houses. For this reason one sees many neoclassical houses with the distinctive architecture of this period. These neoclassical summer houses with gardens consisted the first garden district of Athens, parts of which one can still recognize to date.

Vaso’s house is located in the center of this area (Kypriadou) which is situated very close to the Center but not inside the busy tourist area.

Patission street starts from the center of Athens (it is the extension of Aiolou street which leads to Acropole) and divides Patissia in two areas. Ano Patissia (Upper side Patissia), where Vaso’s house is located, retains many of the characteristic elements of the old Athens (houses with gardens, squares, green sides). Kato Patissia (Lower side Patissia) underwent a rapid urbanization during the 1950’s and today in some parts the effects of the economical crisis are quite evident.

Ano Patissia during the 1980’s and 1990’s was a reference point for the rock stage with many of the classical rock spots still in operation, very close to Vaso’s house.

Patission street is of historical significance for Greece’s contemporary political history. The Polytechnic school and the School of Economics are located on this street, the universities from which the riot against the dictatorship commenced (in 1973).

Vaso’ s house was originally one of these summer villas and was renovated in 1987. The ground floor is built from stone and thus particularly cool during the summer months! It retains many of the characteristics of the old architectural style, with tall ceilings, spacious rooms and a lemon tree garden.

host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

name: Tales in Tiles 1 _  Art Deco flat near Acropolis
description:
In this fully renovated apartment of 1936, you can feel and breath Athens past in a modern set up.
It is spacious and airy. It has a beautiful balcony overlooking St. Nicholas church in front and a very cosy backyard for relaxation.
The neighborhood is quiet and safe, perfect for those who want to get the local feeling. Yet, it is close to Acropolis and in walking distance to all one needs to see and do.

The space
The apartment is located on the first floor of a two-story building, dated back in 1936.
In the entrance hall of the building, on the ground floor, and in this first-floor apartment, one can find all the initial elements of the Art Deco architectural movement of that period: cement tile floors (we have named our apartments after these tiles!), high ceilings, the original windows and shutters.
The apartment on the second floor was an addition of 1957, with remarkably interesting mosaic floors, marble sinks and a private terrace
neighborhood_overview:
Our place is located in a cosy, quiet neighborhood, where you can get a very good feeling of how locals live. The upper part of it is mainly residential, with houses mostly dated in 1930's. Their owners (mainly couples and families - very friendly people) have put a lot of work into renovating them. The community of the church in front is also active and gives a nice touch in the area.
On the other side, the place is very close to good value traditional food places, such as Greek Tavernas and Souvlaki/Gyros places, as well as cafes, breakfast places, bakeries (actually the best bakery in town is there) and everything you may need.
It is c. 10 min walk to the Acropolis hill, c. 15 min walk to the Acropolis Museum and the historical center and c. 20 min walk to the new commercial center.

host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

host_about:
Hi! I am Nefeli, born and raised in downtown Athens, the oldest capital city of Europe! Athens is a straightforward, authentic, lively and resilient city that stands the test of time for centuries. 
I am mother of two, an architect and an artist's estate manager. 
I started hosting in Airbnb because I enjoy meeting new people and I am a fan of travelling and exploring new places. Now after 3 years I still fully enjoy it. 
I also love good food, music, interesting books and witty conversations. 

Fun Mythology Facts:

host_about:
My name is Evangelos but people call me Evan. I studied Art & Design and Architecture in London and after lived and worked there for many years, in house/flat renovations, furniture design and handmade bespoke furniture and a lot more woodworking. After 14 years of creative studies and work i decided to start renovating properties in Athens so i could come back to my country to be even more creative here...back home!

I am a very easy going person, always willing to meet new people, travel, learn and explore new things. Always eager to experience new adventures, places, countries, cultures or even good food. A few things i love and can't do without would have to be the sea, and the harmony and peace that comes with it..the sun and the amazing Greek sunsets/sunrises that you can never get or see enough of them...and there is also my active side and my rush for adrenaline..

 There are quite a few extreme sports that i am in to..such as: off road motorbike riding: enduro and motocross..riding up the mountains to reach the highest point and check out the view..or riding through a dense forest and feel the fresh air, along a river and experience a humid or wet ride or even  down the motocross track for a few laps...i also like to surf and SUP, skate and cycle a lot. In general i like to be active and enjoy life and always up to experience new things!

In the heart of the hippest neighborhood of Athens, just under the Acropolis lies the amazing The Koukaki Residence.

The Koukaki Residence consists of 7 spacious residences, rooms & suites, reflecting the art nouveau ambie
neighborhood_overview:
The Koukaki area, is Athens hippest neighborhood.

Just underneath the Acropolis lies one of the city's most creative and charming corners, nicknamed as Athens ‘Little Paris’.

Koukaki was named after Koukakis, a local bed manufacturer who owned a factory near the historic Sygrou Fix building – which is today home to the National Museum of Contemporary Art. Next to the historic area of Plaka, Koukaki is the closest and most organized district neighboring the Acropolis.

It continues to preserve the glory of its past thanks to the well-preserved and renovated neoclassical homes that represent the Athenian Modernism movement which thrived in the interwar period.
host_about: Part of the Modernism movement and Art Nouveau, The Koukaki Residence abounds in breath taking design elements that will definitely conquer your heart! From the monumental entrance, to the signature stairway which is a work of art of its own, all reflect the nobility of the Greek Bourgeois family who lived in this building at the beginning of the century. All the above encircle the Secret Garden in the middle, which is the Koukaki Residence's best kept secret.

neighborhood_overview:
Attiki is the county in which Athens is located, Greece and home of Attiki station. It is located in the northwest of Athens' centre. The neighbourhood and its central square (Attikis Square) named after Attica Railways, a railway company that constructed the line Athens-Kifissia-Lavrion. Attiki was the terminal station of this line.
Attiki was bounded differently from today in 1908. A clearly urban development of Attiki began in the 1930s with the construction of family houses and the first modern apartment buildings in Athens. The development of apartment buildings was contemporary with Kolonaki and other central neighbourhoods. He writes and illustrates two series of fantasy fiction graphic literature: “The Chronicles of the Archipelago” and “The Chronicles of the West”. 


His painting oeuvre has, until now, been presented at several personal shows in Athens, Kythera Island and Thessaloniki and at several group shows in Montreal, Nicosia, London, Rome, Hamburg, Liverpool, Florence, Athens, Canterbury and New York.


Interests and hobbies

He is a dedicated martial artist. Since 1974 he practices daily Katori Shinto Ryu, Shorin Ryu Karate Do, Matayoshi Kobudo and Fiore dei Liberi.

He tries sincerely to practice Zen Buddhism, Druidism and Shamanism consistently.

He is a passionate amateur scholar of History and Sociology.

He loves reading quality literature and fiction (with an emphasis to Fantasy and Sci-Fi), listening to quality music (mostly Medieval, Renaissance, Classical, Jazz, Old Rock, Ethnic and Electronic) and watching quality movies (among his favourite film-directors Akira Kurosawa, Hayao Miyazaki, the Taviani Brothers,  Luc Besson, Stanley Kubrick, Louis Bunuel, Ridley Scott, Alfred Hitchcock, Lina Wertmüller, Wim Wenders, Martin Scorsese, Quentin Tarantino)

He enjoys greatly hiking on the mountains and in the forests, bicycling, camping outdoors and travelling far and for long (He dreams visiting Latin America, China and Japan).

name: Cozy room in a renovated apartment
description:
The room is part of a spacious, fully equipped, clean and competent apartment, located in the heart of Athens, in Exarcheia. It is easily accessible to public transportation, 10' walking to metro station.
The room is quiet, private and cozy with a window with natural light.
It is really close to Archaeological museum, Lycabettus and Strefis Hill.
Real sense of neighborhood, bookstores, shops, warm cafes and crowded bars, at the historic area of Exarcheia.

The space
The recently renovated apartment is in the 1st floor (with elevator) and consists of three bedrooms, a large living dining room/ kitchen and a bathroom. As I also live in this flat, it has all the appliances you may need for a comfortable stay.
There is burglar alarm, central heating, air condition in the living room, warm water from solar boiler, free wifi, laptop friendly table, washing machine, refrigerator, electric stove, hair dryer, toaster, kettle, moka for espresso.
neighborhood_overview:
Exarcheia is one of Athens’ oldest neighbourhoods and full of life, mainly due to the University of Athens. Because of Exarcheia's liberal history, many artists choose to live here giving an alternative vibe to the area. In addition to the liberal vibe, Exarcheia is a place of free political and social statement with many collectives supporting among other minority.
This authentic neighbourhood is an architectural maze, packed with bohemian shops, shops with handmade products, organic shops, hidden yards. Here you can explore paved alleys with street art, politically charged murals and some of the most unique shops in Athens. You should absolutely visit the graphic flea market where you can see people from all ages knowing each other and shopping on Saturdays.
host_about:
I am a dancer based in Athens. 
As a local, living in the center of Athens, I would happily advise you where to go, what to see and help you with practical information about Athens.

As an artist, I could also advise you about the artistic and alternative scene of Athens! You will have the chance to enjoy theater, dance, music lives that are not well known, in the most underground spaces of Athens! You will find even (why not?) places to have a yoga or dance class!

I love nature and its peacefulness. I like traveling, meeting and socializing with new people! When I don't dance I love reading and cooking!

neighborhood_overview:
Mini-Loft is part of one of the most authentic neighboorhoods of Central Athens, named "Kountouriotika". The Kountouriotika complex was built between 1933 and 1939 to house ethnik Greek refugees from Instanbul and features three rows of Bauhaus buildings. Those buildings, innovative for their time, were the first to incorporate hot water showers. A fire was lit on the top-floor common washing room and pipes were carrying hot water to the residents.

The neighboorhood still remains tight knit, with some refugees and their direct descendants still living in the neighboorhood. Those mix harmonically with young couples that have recently moved into the area, attracting them because of its calm and quiet nature. Essentially you are at the foot Lycabettus hill, the highest greenest hill of Central Athens and can easily walk into Kolonaki, Syntagma and Exarheia areas using the trails at the bottom of Lycabettus Hill park area.
host_about: Having worked and travelled around the world with a backpack and  cycled South America (twice!), I now split my time between my Mini-Loft in Athens and Amorgos , a small island in the Aegean sea where I am a chef and co-owner.  I have refurbished the flat with friends, giving it my own personal touch inspired by my journeys.

Plaka is the “neighbourhood of Gods” with Acropolis above.
The oldest and most picturesque part of Athens, is the ideal location for any visitor.
Plaka is considered the area that developed around the ancient Agora of Athens and is the oldest district in Athens, as it has been continuously inhabited for around three thousand years. Thus, Plaka has a long history and has played an important part in Athenian life, with many famous people having walked along its streets, from Pericles and Alexander the Great to Lord Elgin and Lord Byron, while many well-known Greek writers, actors and artists have lived here, like Giorgos Seferis, Kostis Palamas and Melina Merkouri to name a few.

The Superior Room with balcony consists of two
neighborhood_overview:

host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!

My friends always tell me that they wish they could stay in my place all the time because it makes them feel good and has positive vibes. I do have an optimistic outlook on life, and I also love treating people like royalty, so maybe my home shares some of my qualities. I work as a make-up artist, masseuse and podologist, so I like helping people relax and feel at home. I love meeting new people and interacting with different cultures. In my spare time, I am involved in animal rescue, and I have helped to shelter, feed and find homes for hundreds of stray dogs and cats over the past sixteen years. Many of them required veterinary care because they were abused, malnourished, or sick. 
I take my hosting duties very seriously because I understand that the few days a guest stays at my place may be the only time of the year they can relax and recharge their batteries. Αncient Greeks believed that filoxenia (hospitality) was a sacred duty because the gods disguised themselves as guests and visited them in order to test their kindness. The host and the guests were united with eternal bonds of friendship which their children inherited. This is how I interact with my guests, always taking time to pay attention to individual needs and questions they may have or advice they need to get around. I look forward to welcoming you with a bottle of Greek wine.

Athens is one of the safest cities in the world. What you need to look out for, as in any touristy city, is pickpocketing. This applies especially if you’re going to use the public transport.
Keep your bag in the front of you, not on your back, and always keep your hands on your wallet and cell phone. Separate your travel documents and your money. If you notice a sudden crowd when you’re getting on the bus or the metro, it could be a team of pickpockets – don’t let yourself get distracted. Letting others touch your luggage on public transport is also not recommended.
As for areas to avoid, you should stay out of Omonoia Square, Vathis Square, Kaniggos square and Sofokleous Street – all are hangouts for the homeless, beggars and drug addicts.

host_about:
I am a 30 years old, finishing my master's degree in Global Development Management at the University of Kristiansand, Norway.

What I enjoy most in life is interacting with people and experiencing new things with others. I am curious and open-minded by nature, and love experiencing new food, people and every other experience that nature and culture has to offer.
The hobbies that take up most of my time (next to my studies), relates to challenges which are shared by people regardless of national boundaries, such as; [geo-]politics, conflicts, climate and the 'human condition'.



When it comes to travelling, it is my impression that all destinations that reach a certain amount of popularity, inevitably ends up professionalising tourism and thus hollowing out what visitors would like to experience, leading to commodification rather than natural interactions. As such, I always do my best to seek out the sides, parts and places of any destination that I perceive to be as 'local' as possible - otherwise all that is obtained is people attempting to paint a picture they think one wants to see - rather than the cultured and local experiences one is actually after.

As a general perspective, I prefer to focus on what we as members of this precious planet all share in common, rather than what sets us apart based on differences in culture, religion and our unique traditions. Respect, peace, love and prosperity to all - regardless of any specifications each of us may carry :)

Nestled in the shadow of the Acropolis and more famous districts like Plaka, lies one of the city's most creative and charming corners.

neighborhood_overview:
The flat 'Athena' is centrally located in the area of 'Ambelokipi', (literally meaning ‘vine gardens’), very close to the historical centre of Athens by public transport. Though the area is now a densely populated and completely built urban area, it was indeed once a fully cultivated region full of vineyards many decades ago.
The flat 'Athena' is located right on the very central 'Kifissias' Avenue, a main road artery leading from the centre of Athens to the leafy suburb of Kifissia. It is a busy road boasting many public transport connections to the centre of Athens as well as several suburban naighborhoods around it. A large supermarket can be found almost opposite the building, and a very rich local market with many small high street shops, grocery stores, bakeries and small restaurants can be found on the road behind the building. All in all, most things will be on your doorstep!

It is the lesser-known sister of Makriyianni, which, boasting the elegant Acropolis Museum on the sweeping cobbled esplanade of Dionysiou Areopagitou, has relegated Koukaki to the status of just another residential district.
Yet this unassuming neighborhood has begun to capture the attention of Athenians and visitors alike. For the latter, it is perhaps best known for its staggering popularity as an Airbnb destination, ranking in the top five most interesting neighborhoods in the world to stay. It isn’t difficult to understand why.

host_about:
ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

neighborhood_overview:
The area (Historic Centre) has always been linked to politics and commerce. Commerce remains anchored in this ‘triangle’ with nearby Ermou st. being the protagonist of Athenian retail activity. Though global brands have edged out most of the family-owned shops that used to line the 1.5km long street, you’ll find plenty of smaller niche shops in the side streets.
The perfect starting point for exploring the city on foot or by metro (Monastiraki metro station is a mere 5’ walk away). The city’s booming culinary, café, and bar scene is right at your doorstep as is Varvakeios Market (Athens’s central meat, fish, and vegetable market that dates back to the late 19th century).
Walk the cobblestoned streets from Monastiraki, through Thisseio, Plaka, and up towards Anafiotika. Continue on towards the ancient open-air theatre of Herodeion, the Acropolis Museum, and of course the Acropolis.

movies al fresco. Nearby, the whitewashed homes of the Anafiotika neighborhood give the small enclave a Greek-island vibe.

Το ανακαινισμένο διαμέρισμά μας βρίσκεται σε μια από τις πιο ζωντανές γειτονιές της Αθήνας, στην οποία θα βρείτε καφέ, μπαρ και εστιατόρια κοντά στο κέντρο της πόλης.

The space
Το διαμέρισμα μας στον Κεραμεικό, αν και μικρό, είναι πλήρως λειτουργικό και μοντέρνο. Στην κρεβατοκάμαρα θα βρείτε ένα διπλό κρεβάτι που μετατρέπεται εύκολα σε δύο μονά, αλλά και ντουλάπα για να διατηρείτε εκεί καλοσυντηρημένα τα ρούχα σας. Φρέσκα και καθαρά σεντόνια θα σας περιμένουν κατά την άφιξη σας! Το σαλόνι διαθέτει καναπέ που μπορεί να μετατραπεί σε μικρό μονό κρεβάτι. Σε περίπτωση που θέλετε να μελετήσετε ή να δουλέψετε ο χώρος διαθέτει τραπέζι γραφείου.

Στο μοντέρνο μπάνιο θα βρείτε ντους, τουαλέτα και νεροχύτη, ενώ σας παρέχουμε σαπούνι και σαμπουάν. Στην κουζίνα θα νιώσετε σαν το σπίτι σας, καθώς διαθέτει όλες τις απαραίτητες παροχές όπως ψυγείο, φούρνο, ηλεκτρική κουζίνα βραστήρα και καφετιέρα. Σας προσφέρουμε επίσης επιπλέον παροχές και ποτήρια.

Gues
neighborhood_overview: H περιοχή Κεραμεικός -ή Γκάζι, όπως την αποκαλούν οι ντόπιοι, είναι μία από τις πιο ζωντανές γειτονιές της Αθήνας και βρίσκεται σε κοντινή απόσταση από το Σύνταγμα, την κεντρική πλατεία της χώρας. Είναι δυτικά από την Ακρόπολη και πήρε το όνομα της από τον σημαντικό αρχαιολογικό χώρο που βρίσκεται εδώ: το νεκροταφείο της αρχαίας πόλης των Αθηνών. Εδώ βρίσκεται επίσης η Τεχνόπολη, που κάποτε ήταν εργοστάσιο φωταερίου και σήμερα είναι ένας από τους ωραιότερους πολιτιστικούς χωρους με συναυλίες, εκδηλώσεις και εκθέσεις. Επιπλέον, στην περιοχή θα βρείτε πάρα πολλά εστιατόρια, καφέ και μπαρ για όλα τα γούστα.

The apartment has an excellent location at the foot of Lycabettus hill.
Standing 277 meters above sea level, Lycabettus Hill (also spelt Lykavitos) is the highest point of Athens. The view from Lycabettus Hill is best enjoyed at sunset whilst waiting for the lights of the Acropolis, Temple of Olympian Zeus, Panathenaic Stadium and Ancient Agora to come on. It is worth noting that Athens is surrounded by sea with spectacular views across the Aegean. At the top of the hill you will find the Greek whitewashed church of Agios Georgios (St. George) and all are welcome to enter. The viewing platform in front of the church provides sprawling views of Athens, stretching out to the city’s coastline.

Alexandros.

Uber-centrally located in the heart of historical Athens, this 2019 utterly reconstructed 1-bdr is in the premises of an iconic shoe-factory from the 70’s, which was flipped into a serviced condo-building.

neighborhood_overview:
Psyri, a hip neighborhood, used to have in its premises the majority of the leather traders and craftsmen till the mid 80s’. Now, it has repositioned itself into a vibrant area full of stylish bars, traditional cafes and restaurants.

While walking during the daytime you can meet a variety of people, from businessmen to men selling and bargaining used stuff on the street.

Acropolis, the Acropolis museum, Plaka, Monastiraki flea market, as well as Syntagma square and all the upbeat Athens neighborhoods are in the immediate vicinity.

Upon arrival, we provide you with tailor-made recommendations. Enjoy “Athens by night” while being minutes from home ;)
host_about:
Kalimera (=Good Morning)! I am Alexandros, an ex-financier who turned into an entrepreneur.

Keep it real,
Alexandros.

Hello,
I am Stella " happy traveler" for the last forty years. We decided to do something that we love very much, through AIRBNB.
The Greek word "ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΙΑ=hospitality" is of particular importance in the Greek culture. It’s a compound word from "ΦΙΛΩ=LOVE" and "ΞΕΝΟΣ=GUEST " and refers to the act of nesting and caring for a guest by the host. It was an institution for the ancient Greeks to welcome and take care of the guests at their home. They believed particularly in the idea of hospitality and regarded it as a moral duty and a sacred rule of the gods (Xenios Zeus was the protector of the guests). They offered them bath and sleep and they greeted them with gifts. The host and the guest were linked with friendly ties, which where inherited to their descendants.
This is our inheritance! 
We will be more than glad to host you in our home.

Keramikos has always been an urban Athens neighborhood. Today you can find modern lofts and typical mid-war period houses, influenced by the modernist architecture of the 30s and the 50s and the Bauhaus school.

neighborhood_overview:
Keramikos (or Kerameikos) is named after Keramos, son of Dionysos and Ariadne, hero of the potters. Potters always lived in the area, in the banks of the Eridanos river that used to be here, along with the cemetery of ancient Athens.

Keramikos has always been an urban Athens neighborhood. Today you can find modern lofts and typical mid-war period houses, influenced by the modernist architecture of the 30s and the 50s and the Bauhaus school.
During the recent years Keramikos with the adjacent areas of Gazi and Metaxourgio has been transformed into the ‘hip’ area of Athens. Funky and international cuisine restaurants coexist with traditional taverns, modern bars, countless theaters, museums and gay clubs. An area that remains residential, while becoming a lively neighborhood of the Athens Historical Center, with special events all year round, such as the annual Metaxourgio Carnival Street Party, in the Carnival season.

host_about:
TopHouzzing’s story is simple yet exciting! We are Maria & Alex, the founders, both engineers. So we were already working together in the design & construction sector, so we  dealt with properties all the time. We are both into details, both love doing something right from scratch.

While we were traveling to new places and meeting old friends / making new ones, we felt what a rental should feel like, what it should offer guests like ourselves. Lots were missing, especially the simple little things that makes a visitor feel right at home -away from home. We then decided to start a rentals & real estate management company. It was July 2015 and we named it TopHouzzing Properties - the mission was simply to offer truly top accommodation to our guests. Starting then with a couple of our own properties, refurbished completely, we embarked on a great journey. 

Today the company manages close to 100 properties and growing steadily, mostly in Athens but also in mainland Greece and islands, flats, villas and so on. TopHouzzing  also offers consulting & real estate, design & construction and other professional services in its portfolio.

Hard work and our passion paid off. Our success is clearly stated not only in the many owners that trust us with their properties but even more in the hundreds 5-star reviews from guests from all over the world,  leading us to have a record of 14 consecutive quarters-since the company’s inception- SuperHost status on Airbnb!

We take very good care of our guests and so do we with owners. You see, we both think as guests & owners ourselves. We are waiting anxiously to host you or to manage your property, in both cases you are in good hands with us.

neighborhood_overview:
Petralona is one of the Athens central neighborhoods, situated next to Thissio and Filopapoy Hill. Although very near to the main archeological sites and crowded touristic spots, it is quiet, mainly residential area with small local shops, more resembling the later industrial times. However, like any other part of the city, Petralona has its unique taverns, restaurants and bars frequently visited and well known among Athenians.
A sensitive visitor will catch the authentic, local charm of the place and enjoy relaxing atmosphere around the cafés along the pedestrian zone with children freely playing here and there. This could be an opportunity to learn something about the Athenians’ everyday life.

Safe residential street in Acropolis area . Walking distance to Acropolis and museum. Convenient connection to public transportation, restaurants, coffee shops etc.
Syntagma Square is located directly across from the Greek Parliament Building. Here it is possible to observer the changing of the presidential guard and take pictures with its uniformed members (the Evzones). The square is surrounded by some shops and restaurants and is full of benches where people sit to enjoy the young musicians who often play there. it also marks the start of the 40-acre National garden, south of which is the Zappeion Mansion ( 1874-1888 ). Continuing along from there is the Presidential Mansion ( 1897 ) and the Panathenaic Stadium which is the only stadium in the world built entirely of marble. it is also the place where the first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896. neighborhood_overview:
This upper, hillside part of Koukaki neighborhood, while being extremely central, still keeps its tranquil, residential atmosphere.

host_about: Travelling and exploring new places has always been one of my main passions, along with science and academic research. host_about:
Kalimera, I’m Alex, and welcome to Athens! At Gaia, we encourage our guests to enjoy what the real Greece has to offer and we want to show you that the local way is the only way!

Being Greek, family and hospitality is deeply rooted within our culture, and is at the heart of everything we do here at Gaia. We want our guests to feel right at home in our wonderful city, and however long your stay, we promise to make it a truly enjoyable authentic Greek experience; come and discover what it means to live the local way!

Guests’ safety and comfort is at the top of our list, and we strive to make sure your stay at Gaia meets all your needs as a home from home - we are proud this summer to offer our guests newly renovated rooms, with optimum comfort in mind. I learnt from a young age the value of hospitality and I understand how important it is to feel at home, more than ever when you are away. Growing up with and working in hospitality, I was inspired by my love of meeting new people, making connections, and most of all, helping these people get the most out of their experiences - so much so, that I have formed a career around the business of making this happen! We want to make sure guests don’t just have a place to stay, but gain as much as they can from their visit to Athens! People come from all parts of the world to visit our amazing city as their chosen holiday destination - it’s my job (and my pleasure!) to help make their experience the best it can possibly be!

Athens to me is home; the people, the kindness shown within the community and to strangers alike - we have an amazing atmosphere here, and it’s one you won’t find anywhere else in the world. Here in Athens we like to have fun, we delight in the old and embrace the new - which you’ll see wherever you walk within the city - the beautiful meeting of Modern and Ancient Greece. A city that has it all, everything for everyone - and so much more than a visit to the Acropolis! I want to share this special connection I have with the city with others, and encourage visitors, both Greek and international, to explore the place I’m proud to call home. Let me show you my Athens! 

Psirri in particular, is the buzzing neighbourhood where you’ll find us (along with the best hangouts and eateries in Athens!) - the Gaia family is proud to be part of a community that represents the very soul of the city. Experience real Greece here; eat what the locals do, drink with us, explore our streets you haven’t read about yet, take a walk through our history, modern and ancient - and live the local way!

Since my family and I began constructing Gaia in 2016, we have worked hard to expand, and are now able to offer more options for our guests seeking independent accommodation within the heart of the city. With our guests’ needs in mind, we’re now managing premium apartments, in the perfect location, which capture the authenticity and spirit of Psyri; you’ll be able to experience the real Athens like a local, with all the amenities you need to feel at home.
 
Gaia was created by family for family - since we started out as a small hotel with only a few rooms open, people have loved staying with us because of our incredible culture of going above and beyond when it comes to hospitality - my family has always lived by this principle, and we welcome all of our guests as we do our own family - we’ll make sure you won’t leave Athens without a full stomach, a story to tell and a promise to come back and visit! We look forward to welcoming you soon!
