ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

neighborhood_overview:
Kolonaki area needs no referrals as it is one of the best areas in Athens with lots of choices of coffee shops, restos, retail, bars and museums
As one of the capital's leading shopping areas, it includes a number of high-end boutiques from young adult to casual fashion to prestigious haute couture from Greek and international designers. One of its main shopping streets, Voukourestiou Street, is now known for its jewellery.

Museums and galleries also abound in Kolonaki. The Benaki Museum, inside a preserved neoclassical manor house, and the Goulandris Museum of Cycladic Art and are two of the finest private collections in the country. Two smaller museums to be found in Kolonaki are the Museum of the History of Greek Costume and the Theater Museum, both highly specialized in their respective areas. A walk across the street from Vasilissis Sofias Avenue are the Byzantine Museum, and the War Museum of Athens.

Our company  Ma Maison Y&R owns four luxury apartments in Athens.
We are Yannis and Rena, "fellow travelers" for the last twenty years. Four years ago we decided to do something that we love very much, through BOOKING. 
The Greek word "ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΙΑ=hospitality" is of a particular importance in the Greek culture. It’s a compound word from "ΦΙΛΩ=LOVE" and "ΞΕΝΟΣ=GUEST " and refers to the act of nestling and caring of a guest by the host. It was an institution for the ancient Greeks to welcome and take care of the guests at their home. They believed particularly in the idea of hospitality and regarded it as a moral duty and a sacred rule of the gods (Xenios Zeus was the protector of the guests). They offered them bath and sleep and they greeted them with gifts. The host and the guest were linked with friendly ties, which where inherited to their descendants. 
This is our inheritance.
It will be an honor to host you.

neighborhood_overview: Kaisariani is a family-friendly neighborhood situated around a 30-minute walk from Syntagma square, Panathenaic Stadium and the Temple of Olympian Zeus. Away from the city center’s hustle and bustle, yet close to all main attractions, this quiet area is ideal from those aiming to get a proper taste of local life in Athens. Adjacent to Pagrati, an upcoming neighborhood with a vibrant nightlife, Kaisariani is surrounded by numerous restaurants, cafes and bars. The area’s trademark is Skopeftirio Grove, a 14-acre urban park painted with cobblestoned alleys, pine trees, firs and cypresses, ideal for a relaxing walk or an outdoor picnic. A shooting range during World War II,  the area was transformed into a park featuring playgrounds, an open-air cinema and a cozy cafe in 1984. A memorial built in honor of the victims of the German occupation stands in the heart of the park bearing testimony to the place’s historical significance.

Το διαμέρισμα βρίσκεται στην όμορφη περιοχή του Παγκρατίου, κοντά στο κέντρο της πόλης, σύγχρονο και ιστορικό. Η άλλοτε αστική περιοχή έχει μετραταπεί σε σημείο συνάντησης νέων ανθρώπων, με εύκολη πρόσβαση στην αγορά, σε σουπερμαρκετ, καφέ, εστιατόρια, διατηρώντας ακόμα την αίσθηση και την ασφάλεια μιας παλιάς γειτονιάς. Η πρόσβαση στο κέντρο της πόλης γίνεται εύκολα και με τα πόδια αλλά και με μέσα μεταφοράς. Ιδανική επιλογή για επισκέπτες που έρχονται για εργασία, για οικογένειες και ζευγάρια.

The space
Το διαμέρισμα , 60 τ.μ, βρίσκεται στον 1ο όροφο και διαθέτει 2 υπνοδωματια, καθιστικό, κουζίνα και μπάνιο. To πρώτο υπνοδωμάτιο έχει διπλό κρεββάτι, ντουλάπες για τα προσωπικά σας αντικείμενα και πρόσβαση στο μπαλκόνι. Βρίσκεται δίπλα από το καθιστικό, το οποίο έχει επίσης πρόσβαση στο μπαλκόνι, και την κουζίνα η οποία είναι πλήρως εξοπλισμένη ώστε να ετοιμάζετε τα γεύματά σας. Διαθέτει ψυγείο, φούρνο και εστίες, φούρνο μικροκυμάτων και τις απαραίτητες παροχές.
neighborhood_overview: Μία παλιά Αθηναϊκή γειτονιά η οποία έχει γίνει σημείο συνάντησης νέων και δημιουργικών ανθρώπων. Τα τελευταία χρόνια το Παγκράτι έχει γνωρίσει μια νέα άνθιση. Θα βρείτε εστιατόρια, καφετέριες, σουπερμάρκετ, μπαρ αλλά και στούντιο καλλιτεχνών. Εντός μικρής απόστασης βρίσκεται το Καλλιμάρμαρο και ο Εθνικός Κήπος. The National Archaeological Museum of Athens, the National Technical University of Athens and Strefi Hill are all in walking distance. The central square features many coffee shops and bars with numerous retail computer shops located mainly on Stournari street, also called the Greek Silicon Valley.

neighborhood_overview:
The building stands in downtown Athens, at the heart of the downtempo and almost communal neighborhood of Metaxourgeio, some 5 minutes walk from the metro station with the same name.
Located between Gazi with its famed nightlife and busy Omonia Sq., Metaxourgeio is a residential area that attracts many visitors. The neighborhood has acquired a reputation as an artistic and fashionable place due to the opening of many art galleries, theaters, trendy restaurants and cafes. Albeit being frequented by the hip youths of Athens, here you will find no posh or fancy clubs, but innumerable little raki places, where you can order meze to enjoy on the traditional tavern chairs set on the pavement; expect also to find hip little bars and some of the best street food corners and street art of the city. Moreover, the neighborhood gives visitors a budding sense of community that makes everything even more homey.

host_about:
I am from Athens, however I have very close ties with two beautiful Greek islands Santorini and Patmos.

As my father’s family is from Santorini I spent all my summers there. Since I am a licensed tour guide, in 2004 I decided to move to Santorini in order to work there. This was a great chance to start renovating my family’s properties in order to be able to share them with people from all over the world. 

In addition, many years ago, my mother visited the island of Patmos, fell in love with it and decided to buy two beautiful pieces of land, including very old farmhouses in ruinous condition, that she slowly renovated. In this way, our family and numerous friends enjoyed many unforgettable Patmos Easters and summers. Nowadays, I am responsible for the good condition of the houses that I rent out and share the beauty and special ambiance of this island with our guests.

I am very lucky since my twin daughters, Alexandra and Christina, having completed their studies abroad in hospitality management and tourism, returned to their roots in order to continue and develop what I started.  Genuine hospitality, love and respect for the island, as well as the embracement of the local culture define our core values. Nowadays we all share our time between Santorini, Patmos and Athens, and have the honor and pleasure to share our family’s story and our love for these islands, with visitors from all over the world. 

After many years in the hospitality industry, today I have the pleasure along with my daughters to embrace one more much loved island home, my husband's summer house on the island of Hydra. The house was built by my father in law 40 years ago. My husband Dimitris will be managing the house in Hydra.

Thissio is the name of a traditional neighborhood in Down-town Athens, northwest of the Acropolis, 1.5 km southwest of downtown. Long ago, the name was derived from the Temple of Hephaestus which was mistakenly known as Thiseion in refer-ence to Theseus, the mythical king of Athens, which gave rise to the neighborhood being named Thissio.
It is surrounded by hills, heights and historical sites which are within a walking distance. The Ancient Agora of Athens, Stoa of Attalos, the Temple of Hephaestus and Kerameikos Archae-ological Museum can be entered from Thissio; all others, the National Observatory of Athens, Acropolis of Ath-ens, Philopappos Monument, Mouseion Hill, Pnyx, which is con-sidered the birthplace of Democracy, and the Mount Lycabet-tus can be easily reached or viewed from Thissio. neighborhood_overview:
Within 5 minutes’ walk is the main entrance of the Acropolis Temple, Parthenon, Kalimarmaron Stadium and Plaka.
The Acropolis Museum is an archaeological museum focused on the findings of the archaeological site of the Acropolis of Athens. The museum was built to house every artifact found on the rock and on the surrounding slopes, from the Greek Bronze Age to Roman and Byzantine Greece.
In the shadow of the Acropolis and its ancient temples, hillside Plaka has a village feel, with narrow cobblestone streets lined with tiny shops selling jewelry, clothes and local ceramics. Nearby, the whitewashed homes of the Anafiotika neighborhood give the small enclave a Greek-island vibe.
The nearest airport is Eleftherios Venizelos Airport.

Ermou street is a commercial avenue which has been turned into a pedestrian only street. Off Aeolou Street just a couple blocks NW of Ermou is the Church of Agia Irini, which used to be the main cathedral of Athens until they built the new cathedral on Metropolis Street (which is now falling down.) Next to Agia Irini is a square which used to be full of flower shops but now only one or two remain. The shops have been replaced by cafes which are among the best places to go for coffee in the morning, a beer or snack in the afternoon, and at night they are abuzz with young people when they turn into bars. neighborhood_overview:
Pagrati is located 15 minutes walking distance from the centre of Athens.

Named after the ancient sanctuary of Hercules it is also known as the culture/ arts district of Athens, home to Greece's best artistic talent, the Olympic Stadium, Spondi (Michelin star restaurant), one of the most beautiful parks (Kallimarmaro), the recently opened Goulandris Museum (with an extensive collection of Greek as well as art greats such as Picasso, Monet, Gogh, Gauguin, Monet and Cezanne).

Take a stroll down to the First Cemetery of Athens or the platia to witness some world class talent performing.

In addition, the food is world class, whether it be vegetarian (Baba Ghanoush), delicious cakes or patisseries (Oh Boy) or simply coffee (Olivers) make sure to take some time to explore how the locals live.

host_about:
ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

There aren’t many places which showcase so perfectly the multi-layered mix of cultures which we call Greek civilization, like Monastiraki square. It is situated north of Plaka, the traditional neighborhood under the Acropolis, and right next to the busy junction of two central streets, Ermou and Athinas.
Where does Monastiraki name comes from?
The name ‘Monastiraki’, which means ‘small monastery’, refers to the orthodox monastery that occupied the square during the Ottoman times. The only remnant today is the church mentioned above and, of course, the tell-tale name of the neighborhood. The addition of the Mosque in the 18th century fueled the economic growth of the surrounding area, making the Monastiraki market a stable feature of the area up until today.

neighborhood_overview:
Athens Green Apartments are located in the central Athens district of Pangrati next to Panathenaic Stadium (know as Kallimarmaro where the fisrt modern Olympic Games in 1896 took place), to the east of the National Gardens and the Zappeion Exhibition Hall, to the west of the Pangrati residential district and between the twin pine-covered hills of Ardettos and Agra. Up to the 1950s, the Ilissos River (now covered by, and flowing underneath, Vasileos Konstantinou Avenue) ran in front of the stadium's entrance, and the spring of Kallirrhoe, the sanctuary of Pankrates (a local hero) and the Cynosarges public gymnasium were nearby.

The Fokianos sports facility lies across Vasileos Konstantinou Avenue, and adjacent to it are located the Athens tennis club, the Ethnikos athletics track, the Federation swimming pool, the remnants of the Temple of Olympian Zeus, and Hadrian's Gate.

description:
Located in the most vibrant and interesting neighbourbood in the centre of Athens, this home offers a true local experience with everything you need at your doorstep. The house itself, positioned in one of the best streets in Exarcheia is very spacious, full of natural light and provides every comfort one requires after exploring Athens and its many wonders.

The space
There are two bedrooms (one queen bed and one double bed), a fully equipped kitchen and a spacious living area to lounge in. The wraparound balcony offers a wonderful opportunity to observe the rythym of local Athenians.
The accommodation includes wifi, smart tv with Netflix option, hotel quality linen, air con, washing machine and is aesthetically minimally decorated.
neighborhood_overview:
Exarcheia is known as the heartbeat of Athens. Its tree lined streets are filled with cafes, bars, restaurants, traditional greek tavernas, bookstores, music stores, artists, intellectuals and students.

From the apartment, it is a very brief walk to the magnificent views of Athens from Lykavittos and Strefi hill. Within 10 minutes you will find yourself at Panepistimiou or Omonia metro station.

The National Archaelogical Museum of Athens is within walking distance as is Syntagma square, and the surrounding neighbourhoods of Kolonaki, Monastiraki, Psirri and Plaka. At 2.8kms away, the Acropolis can also be visited by foot. The beauty of this house and its location is that whilst situated in the centre of Athens, it uniquely still embodies the essence of a community and a traditional neighbourhood.

Every Saturday, very close by is the renowned Exarcheia/ Kalllidromiou farmers market, with fresh fruit, vegetables, olives, honey , fish and more.

host_about:
Our company  Ma Maison Y&R owns four luxury apartments in Athens.
We are Yannis and Rena, "fellow travelers" for the last twenty years. Four years ago we decided to do something that we love very much, through BOOKING. 
The Greek word "ΦΙΛΟΞΕΝΙΑ=hospitality" is of a particular importance in the Greek culture. It’s a compound word from "ΦΙΛΩ=LOVE" and "ΞΕΝΟΣ=GUEST " and refers to the act of nestling and caring of a guest by the host. It was an institution for the ancient Greeks to welcome and take care of the guests at their home. They believed particularly in the idea of hospitality and regarded it as a moral duty and a sacred rule of the gods (Xenios Zeus was the protector of the guests). They offered them bath and sleep and they greeted them with gifts. The host and the guest were linked with friendly ties, which where inherited to their descendants. 
This is our inheritance.
It will be an honor to host you.

neighborhood_overview:
Shila is centrally located in the chic neighbourhood of Kolonaki, nestled in a quiet pedestrianised street, moments away from downtown Athens.

The area is one of the most vibrant in Athens and has become a go-to for Athenians looking for the best in fashion, art, food, nightlife and live music.

It’s also a cultural hub with a wide selection of art and history museums including; The Benaki Museum, Museum of Cycladic Art and the B&E Goulandris Foundation.

As an escape from the city, Mount Lycabettus is easily accessible by foot and offers great hiking opportunities and views of the city and the Acropolis is just a short ride away.
host_about:
Shila is an ethereal late 1920s residence in the heart of Athens, which brings new meaning and inspiration to the concept of the boutique hotel.  A place to feel indulged and at home, and yet at the same time, to experience an otherworldly realm of elegance and sensuality. 

Combining elements of the bygone and the contemporary– and reminiscent of a hotel particulier – this neoclassical house comprises of six distinctively designed suites, each unique in character, with a unifying element of simplicity and sexy charm.

Shila features a lush courtyard, a tranquil rooftop, lounging areas and reading nooks, ideally suited for social gatherings, art happenings and private events.  We offer the ultimate curated experience in culinary, art, design, and indulgent self-care. An invitation to experience our intuitive hospitality, where Shila stands as a magnetic universe of its own.

name: Downtown Junior Suite by LOFUS bio-suites
description:
A unique accommodation proposal in the heart of Athens.

LOFUS bio-suites combine urban hospitality with elements of biophilic design and island architecture.

They are easily accessible as they are located within a short distance from Metro central stations. It is an ideal location as it is close to the famous tourist attractions of Athens, entertainment venues, and the most known shopping pedestrian street of the capital.

The space
Each Junior Suite by LOFUS bio-suites has a surface of 35 m², including an open-plan bright space in Greek-island style with touches of biophilic design.

It consists of a sleeping area, a comfortable bathroom, a seating area and a work desk.

The room is equipped with a small fridge, kettle, Nespresso machine, hairdryer, body scale, safe box , and a flat screen TV with Youtube, Amazon Prime Video and Netflix options.

Free toiletries from 100% recyclable packaging, linens and slippe
neighborhood_overview:
LOFUS bio-suites are located in close vicinity to the high shopping streets and popular areas in the heart of Athens center.

You can reach the Monastiraki area with many tavernas (traditional Greek food options) as well as alternative dining options and a large flea market, at just 300 meters walking distance.

Moreover, the most popular shopping street in Greece, which is Ermou Street, is located at just 5-minute walking distance.

Additional popular sites near the accommodation are the “Roman Agora” and, of course, the most remarkable monument of Greece, “Acropolis of Athens”.

Distances to Transport Hubs

- Athens Internation Airport at 35 km.

- Rafina Port (ferries mostly to the “Cyclades” island-complex) at 30 km.

- Piraeus Port (ferries to all Aegean islands) at 12 km.

- Nearest Metro station (“Monastiraki” station) at just 300 meters.

- “Omonoia” Metro station at 700 meters.

host_about:
ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

host_about:
Geia sas! Hey I’m Fotini. My name is the Greek version of Clara, Claire, Kiara or even in Russian Svetlana. And it means bright and shiny it has to do with light even with enlightenment. Hopefully I will, if you wish, shed some light on your unique stay in Athens.
A bit about me personally! I run my own business as a freelance professional, I’m a mum to my 12-year-old daughter who keeps me on my toes and then some! I was born in Germany and I have spent almost 25 years of my life in Germany in different cities. But I have called Athens home for almost 20 years now. I truly love this place and feel very, very lucky to live in Athens/Greece– it’s more than all right here!
I have been working as a conference interpreter since 1997 and I also share my Athens in personalized tours for quite some time now. I have met and worked with many different types of people, from all walks of life in all these years. I like communicating with people and as a host I love to share my passion about this amazing city, the city of Athens. There are so many stories, legends, myths, so many places to see and experience. Athens is the place to be. History, unique sights, lots of hidden gems, exceptional food experiences, the Sea, our Athens Riviera, and of course warmhearted people. 
As your bilingual host I would love to welcome you and be a part of your experience in Athens. To share my city with you. I would love to become your host and to give you lots of insights. I hope to see you soon.

Our area belongs to the city of Athens, but at the same time, it looks like a suburb, as it is a quiet and safe residential area with a lot of green and buildings separated one from the other. We are 800 meters away from metro station PANORMOU (check that station on the map), where you can find a lot of amusement centers. host_about:
Hello, I am Ira and I live in Athens, Greece.
I have studied and worked in various fields, such as media, events, education and modern ways of marketing. I have traveled in Europe and the USA and I have lived in Barcelona and Istanbul.

I love to communicate with people and always meet new. I get inspired by the success and leadership of others, both in big matters and in everyday life. I enjoy gatherings with friends, romantic moments, good coffee and nice places to visit. My favorite food is pasta, my everyday sweet is chocolate, my best season is spring. Life moto: The distance between dreams and reality is called action.

After I met my husband, George, we have been involved together in several interesting and intensive experiences, related to business and public awareness. 
It was in 2015 when we traveled abroad for a project and we found out about Airbnb. After using it as guests, we liked the idea a lot and we starting hosting.  

Within the second month, we became Superhosts and within 2 years, we have hosted more than 700 times, in homes that we personally renovated, decorated and totally prepared for our guests from all around the world. 

In January of 2018, we went beyond and started a company in order to focus 100% on creating top quality homes and offering a top quality hosting to our guests. Its name is DIAMOND HOMES. Our aim is to create more and more small diamonds in the city and to welcome more and more people in them. 

We are expecting you in sunny and magical Athens! Explore our listings!

host_about:
ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

Although it has been a working class area when walking around one can admire the architecture of the neoclassical buildings of the 19th and early 20th century that were constructed for the business owners of the time.

host_about:
My name is Eftihia (Eftehea), from the words 'ef' and 'tihi' (tehe) which mean 'good' and 'luck' in ancient greek. My name is also a noun. In modern greek the word eftihia means happiness. For ancient greeks happy was the fortunate one. Nowdays happy is the joyful one. My name is quite a heavy thing to go by everyday, as it means something so great and simple (but veeeery complicated too..), that it is sometimes a real struggle to deliver its meaning and idea and project in in your life. And other's lives around you.

My parents origins are from the Peloponese and Zakynthos (Ionian Island). But I grew up in the wider terretory of Attica Prefecture, in particular in 2 suberbs of Athens- Marousi and Kifisia.

My profession is acting and as that started as a career (B.C. - before Crisis!!!) but has practically ended up a practical hobby (A.C.- after Crisis..), I am trying to reinvent myself and my life and scetch a 'plan B'..

Whatever that will occur to be, my true passion is walking barefoot on sharp rocks of isolated greek islands. If I was from India I think they would say I used to be a wild goat in a previous life. My technique in this strange extreme sport is really something to admire. I love walking in general, I like nature and even though I am definately a child of the city, my soul meets its 'core' when away from it. It is like the purity of my existence absolutely relates to the inviroment I find myself in. The landscape of a mountain or a beach or a lake or a river automatically turns me into a better person. My effort has always been to manage to carry that person with me even in the packed and trafficy Streets and Avenues of Athens.

My favourite time of the day in the area I leave in (where my house that welcomes airbnb guests is located) is between 2-6 in the morning. When the city sleeps one is able to 'pick up' and fully absorb this area's true energy. When crowded it is just another touristic place with great historical interest. But its healing effect one can only get when it is (Website hidden by Airbnb) and (Website hidden by Airbnb) l.. At times of grief, pressure or distress I found that walking (AND jogging too!) around in that neighbourhood at these hours of the day was very therapeutic.

Sharing your house with people you don't know (and- at circummstances- you might actually never even meet!!!) became possible thanks to this whole airbnb notion that you created. It is a beautiful chain that connects people who wanted more- out of traveling- than a regular hotel or rudimantary furnished/equipped apartments. That chain allows travellers to make a 'subtour'  in their tour, experience how a person from a different country and culture lives. Like a quick whimsy eavesdropping or innocent peeping that might 'salt or sweeten up' the first and last moments of ones journey to a foreign place. 

So.. Long live the AirBnB!

host_about:
ABOUT ME  
I grew up in Athens, Greece and I decided to become a full-time Airbnb host in 2014 at the age of 28. Hospitality has always been something that I have been passionate about. I was in the music industry for many years. I hosted music events in Athens, which gave me the ability to easily interact with all types of people. Making the people around me feel good has become my core passion and purpose.

MY AIRBNB STORY 
2011 
I took a one way trip to Ibiza, Spain for self-discovery. I ended up spending 9 months on this beautiful Balearic island meeting awesome people, struggling, and working at the very well known Cafe Del Mar. Of course, this journey had its ups and downs. I'd be more than happy to describe them over coffee with you.

2012 
After Ibiza, I decided to forego the nightlife and focus on finishing my studies and accomplishing my mandatory Army duty in Greece.  

2014 
After finishing my studies in Computer Science, I ended up spending 6 months as a soldier in Cyprus.  The last 3 days before my departure back to Greece I took on the challenge to book an Airbnb for the very first time. My host, Nicolas, blew my mind with his extraordinary kindness and hospitality. As you can probably guess, that was my starting point for hosting.  

2014 UNTIL TODAY 
I have hosted more than 3,000 happy guests, shared beautiful human moments, gained financial freedom, traveled the world, became an official Airbnb public speaker, recruited and helped more than 40 new Airbnb hosts, and assisted more than 150 guests with unexpected travel issues (stolen passports, missed flights, etc).  

MY VISION 
I want to continue building my personal hospitality brand (withPanos), offer the best local experiences, create a well-being movement, share many Greek meals, travel the world, explore hospitality through kindness, and maybe one day become a proud father and spouse.  

INTERESTS 
My interests include: spiritual and personal development; running; biking; swimming; traditional Greek food; tea; gardening; reading/listening to books; taking care of my backyard wildlife; exploring the USA; and cooking (when I have the time to enjoy it). I am passionate about languages and learning. I am fluent in English and I am learning Spanish and German. I previously studied Computer Science. I am enthusiastic about human connection, listening to people’s stories, and spiritual connection. I am also passionate about dogs and nature.  

FAVORITE MUSIC, MOVIES & BOOKS 
I love music and enjoy anything from Classical to Funk, R&B, Motown, the Beatles, Classic Rock, Blues, Pop, New Age, Country, and just about anything, although I am not as well versed in Hip Hop.  Shawshank Redemption, West Side Story . . . there are so many movies I love; it just depends on my mood. I typically watch inspirational movies, true stories, documentaries, romance, dramas, period movies, martial arts, and animation. I prefer movies that are not overly violent. I have a sense of humor and loved the movie "Under Cover Brother." I like Tyler Perry movies.  I read a lot of spiritual, inspiration, and business books. I enjoy Pema Chodron and often refer to “The Power of Now” by Eckhart Tolle. I recently read "The Surrender Experiment,” “The Glass Castle,” and “Your Brain at Work." I listen to audiobooks constantly which is how I get through so many books so quickly.  

COUNTRIES I'VE VISITED 
United States, Canada, UK, France, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Sweeden, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania.  

TRAVELING STYLE & HOSTING 
I am an adventurous traveler. I prefer to do and see things the locals enjoy. I prefer not to travel in groups or take cruises. I can be flexible and enjoy a range of accommodations and meals, but in general I like to keep things simple.  As a host, however, I enjoy guests who love to interact with the locals. I always make sure they feel well cared for — even spoiled. My guests enjoy my fun approach to life, as well as my interactive blackboards and world maps. I have always been complimented on my eye for detail and my desire to make even the ordinary feel special.  From the lovely views, peaceful settings, and friendly outdoor animal visitors, to the manner in which I go out of my way to make things unique and fulfill guest requests, you can count on having a positive stay and looking forward to a return visit to our beloved homes in exciting Athens.

Hugging the base of the Acropolis, the area extends from Filomousson Square, roughly at the intersection of Kidathinaion and Adrianou Streets, down to Monastiraki. The best way to see Plaka is to simply wander its lanes, chasing glimpses of the Acropolis between the neoclassical buildings, Byzantine churches, cafes, restaurants, and souvenir shops. The prime sights are, of course, the Parthenon and the Acropolis Museum. neighborhood_overview:

Recently , an interesting part of Ottoman landmarks has reopened which add to the list of sightseeing . The main shopping area of Ermou, Monastiraki square and the designer shops on Adrianou street are a mere 10 min walk . Ice cream stands, antique shops and hand woven rug shops add to your shopping sprees.
In the evening , many terraces offer a bird’s eye view of the city but you could always enjoy a glass of wine at your private leisure.

neighborhood_overview: Everything you need is here and the historic center is an easy 10 - 20 minute walk depending on your route. You'll find grocers, restaurants & cafes at your doorstep as well as Athens' newest art museum, the Old Olympic Stadium and the National Gardens.
host_about:
Who would have thought when I boarded a plane for Greece more than 20 years ago, planning on backpacking through the mountains and then heading north through then Yugoslavia I'd end up making Greece my second home?
But here I am, 20 something years later, running a fabulous Greek vacation rental business with historic homes & penthouses in Athens, planning Greek travel itineraries and leading small group food & wine focused tours around my adopted homeland and loving the life that I am lucky enough to be living. Of course I did pick up an equally crazy, workaholic Greek husband along the way, as well as a stray Greek animal or two!

Update: End of November 2017 .... This year Basil and I celebrate 15 years opening our Greek vacation rentals to guests from around the world. All these years we've been hopping between Basil's home city, Athens and Carole's home city of Chicago.  Time and time again guests in Greece ask us if they can stay in our Chicago home while we're in Athens.... so we're finally doing it - we've just completed the renovation of a fab old factory with 3 vacation rentals called the Magic Factory Lofts. We've got 3 and 4 bedroom homes in the heart of the city with Big Shoulders -  in our hybrid warehouse (which in a previous life housed a bar and a dance hall, followed by a costume and magic card factory and then a photography studio where probably every Butterball turkey advertisement in the 1980s was shot .... the photos, not the turkeys!)

So come stay with us ... and then stay with us again. Whether we share an ouzo in Athens in our Acropolis View Alpha Plus penthouse or Sky Villa or a beer and a hot dog in Chicago, in our Magic Factory Lofts  we know that you won't be disappointed.
